replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I rarely feel anxious about math. My vocational training and early exposure to chemistry helped build confidence. Anxiety tends to come when problems are too complex or time-sensitive, but I’ve learned to approach them calmly and methodically.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I haven’t used AI for math learning recently. As a retired person with a vocational background, I prefer hands-on practice and older methods like textbooks. I find AI tools too new and not aligned with my learning style.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If it’s positive, you get two real solutions; if zero, one real solution; if negative, complex numbers. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f’(x). Set f’(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are critical points. Then plug them back into f(x) to find the corresponding y-values. Check if they are maxima or minima using the second derivative test.
